chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from some of our companions, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them):

Regarding a man who married two sisters in a single contract, he said: 'He has the choice to keep whichever he wishes and release the other.' And whoever contracted marriage with a woman and then contracted with her sister afterwards, then the contract with the second is invalid, so he should keep the first.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man marries two sisters at the same time in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the juristic distinction between simultaneous and sequential marriage to two sisters, a key topic in Shia fiqh regarding the validity of the second union. It establishes that while a man may choose to retain either sister if married in a single contract, a sequential marriage renders the second contract void (*batil*), requiring him to keep the first. This ruling underscores the principle that the prohibition of two sisters is absolute in terms of cohabitation, but the contractual mechanics differ based on the timing of the *aqd*.
